title: Injection provenance: local-only storage for List-ID-routed articles
description:
Tag every article with its injection source and use that to decide whether it enters the group log (peerable via IHAVE/TAKETHIS) or stays reader-local only.

Why this issue exists:
Articles injected from email via List-ID routing are locally filed email messages, not Usenet articles. Propagating them via IHAVE/TAKETHIS to peers is wrong: it pollutes the Usenet feed with mailing list traffic and risks duplicates if peers also receive the same emails via their own SMTP relay.

Routing policy:
  NntpPost        (NNTP POST command)                    → group log + IPFS  (peerable)
  SmtpNewsgroups  (SMTP with explicit Newsgroups: header) → group log + IPFS  (peerable)
  SmtpSieve       (SMTP routed by sieve fileinto)         → group log + IPFS  (peerable)
  SmtpListId      (SMTP routed by List-ID fallback)       → IPFS + reader tables only (local)

Implementation:
- InjectionSource enum in core
- Source flows through NntpQueue envelope (SMTP path) and direct POST path
- Reader ingest pipeline branches: group log entry written only for peerable sources
- Group log entry gains informational injection_source field for the peerable cases
- Transit peering unaffected: it only replicates the group log, which never contains SmtpListId articles
